title: Orphan Session Attribution Convergence and Cost Boundary Reconciliation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several customers reported intermittent spikes and negative deltas in monthly bills traced to short-lived sessions and streaming requests that never reconciled into the canonical token ledger. Investigation shows: 1) a subset of session fragments are emitted without stable session IDs when requests route through legacy proxy paths; 2) our realtime fanout occasionally drops finalization events under transient backpressure; and 3) the compaction job that canonicalizes per-request fragments is non-idempotent and times out under peak load, leaving orphaned token fragments. This ticket implements a convergence service to compact and re-attach orphan fragments to canonical sessions, apply deterministic cost boundary rules, and emit idempotent reconciliation delta records for downstream billing jobs.
acceptance_criteria: Convergence service compacts >99.9% of fragments for test datasets (24-hour replay) without introducing duplicates
Reconciliation deltas are idempotent and consume <= 10ms per record on average in steady state
End-to-end test shows monthly bill delta for synthetic tenants falls within expected error budget (<0.2%)
New Grafana dashboard surfaces orphan fragment rate, compaction latency, and reconciliation delta counts
Backfill tool successfully reconciles 30 days of historical orphaned fragments for staging cluster with human review checklist
comments: 2026-02-25 - Triage: Asha - flagged by Customer Ops after ticket from Acme Analytics. Reproduced in staging with replay data; high priority due to billing exposure.
2026-02-27 - Spike: Liam O'Connor - ran a 48h replay and confirmed 0.6% of tokens are in orphan fragments; majority from streaming path v1.2. Noted PK collision cases and missing finalization events.

2026-03-02 - Design review: Team agreed on two-phase approach: (1) lightweight converger that uses deterministic fingerprinting + TTL window to attach fragments; (2) longer-running compactor for historical backfill with snapshot isolation.

2026-03-05 - Blocker identified: schema change required for reconciliation record idempotency. Coordinating with infra for brief migration window. See Confluence design: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/987654321/Orphan+Session+Attribution
2026-03-08 - PR opened for converger prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123 - includes integration tests and a synthetic replay harness.
2026-03-10 - QA: Added chaos test for transient backpressure; converger gracefully retries, metrics emitted. Noted a memory spike at 1.2M fragments; optimization planned.
2026-03-12 - Next: schedule migration on 2026-03-18 staging, then small-customer canary on 2026-03-19 before full rollout. Assigned follow-ups to eng infra for autoscaling policy tuning.
implementation_notes: Converger runs as a k8s CronJob with sharded partition key (customer_id mod N) to limit memory footprint
Deterministic fingerprint uses (customer_id, route_fingerprint, truncated_timestamp, sequence_hash) to attach fragments across retries
Emit reconciliation records to kafka topic billing.reconciliation.deltas with exactly-once semantics via producer-side dedupe keys
Backfill will use snapshot isolation on parquet snapshots and write to a staging topic for human review before final commit
runbook: If converger job fails during a run: 1) Pause the cron to prevent retry storms. 2) Inspect last successful offset in Kafka topic billing.input.fragments. 3) Run dry-mode compaction against a 6-hour window in staging and verify metrics. 4) If memory OOMs observed, scale deploy to next shard count and restart. 5) After fix, re-run backfill in small batches and monitor billing.orphan_fragments.rate and reconciliation.delta_error_rate. Contacts: on-call eng for billing (pager: #billing-oncall).
notes_for_release_notes: Added a converger to reduce orphaned token fragments and improve billing accuracy. Initial rollout will run in canary mode for selected tenants; billing deltas expected to be reduced to within error budget.
qa_plan: 1) Unit and integration tests for deterministic fingerprinting and idempotency. 2) Staging replay for 72 hours of production traffic. 3) Chaos test (inject lost-finalization events). 4) Small-customer canary for 48h, compare invoices and internal delta metrics.
expected_risks: Schema migration could cause brief consumer lag; converger memory pressure under worst-case fragmentation; risk of false-positive merging if fingerprint collision threshold too permissive.
